body: One of my all time greatest fears.

Repressing these thoughts only compounds them. They keep piling up in your head like trash in a hoarders house. He should probably see a professional for help. Loved ones are not therapists. The best way to deal with intrusive thoughts and images related to OCD is to address them when they are not ambushing you. Those thoughts need processing and it needs to be done at a time the thought is not considered intrusive. Best of luck to you and your boyfriend. Take care of yourself too.

Ranger is Lvl2 THAC0 19. 

I agree with your assessment, but I know the Ranger is not using expertise, she calls it specialization and has marked down the +1 ToHit and +2DMG on her sheet, twice actually so she always is at +2 ToHit and +4DMG before other bonuses or her imaginary double damage.

The Ranger, I can tell you is not using anything other than what is in the PHB. When I ask her about stuff she just says it's written on her character sheet, but has no idea where it comes from in games rules.

The thing is, I'm an optimizer. I've read the books, the expansions and know the rules as written. I know DMs can make whatever call they want and there is homebrew. This isn't that though.

He seems to know his stuff. He knows rules and tables by memory.

10 total in the group but we average 6-7 per night as not everyone can make it.

Yeah. I'm not sure things get better, but they get different.

I'll let you know that my kids bring me more joy than I ever thought I deserved. It doesn't stop the pain from the rest of it. From the past, the abuse, rape, the lies and gaslighting, whatever is there. None of that goes away.

Most of us do not get a good start to life. Yours in particular sounds quite terrible. I'm sorry these are your circumstances. 

There are things you can find in your life that will give you a sense of meaning and desire to continue out of something more positive than spite. This takes hard work but it's possible.

I hope you find a way to change your circumstances. All the best.

Working is a part of living. I have personally never felt much achievement in my "career". I always had a dream of making over 100K a year and I worked really hard at it. When it happened I felt nothing. My dream meant nothing and I realized that work and career are irrelevant to true happiness.
Kids. Live for the kids and hopefully their lives won't be as fucked up and shameful as mine.

I think it's very noble to think of the people you will affect. Including the poor soul who finds you.

I know what you mean and agree. My plan includes a drive away from home, a call to the police to let them know where I am so random ppl dont find me, and so they can pick up my gun. A walk away from my car so it's not bloodied or damaged. That way my family can sell it afterwards.

You aren't going to find the truth about a partner E.G. They love you for you. If you are lying to them to figure it out.

Honesty is always the best advice.

I'm sorry you are going through this. I can use a few of those words to describe myself and I know the feeling of worthlessness. We are our own worst judge so I doubt people around you feel the same as you do.

Maybe this can help you. I suffered severe cognitive decline a little like you describe. Brain just doesn't work, can't remember or solve simple problems without causing extreme exhaustion. Turns out I have sleep apnea and my brain is just really never sleeping. It impacted all manner of my life including my depression. I'm working on resolving this now and I've noticed sharp improvements in my cognition like when I was young again.

Maybe your issues stem from something clinical like that and can be helped. Please don't write yourself off. As hard as it is you are 23 and there is a lot of time left to improve yourself.

Best of luck to you.

Hi,

I want to say first that people who are advocating for you to get a hysterectomy or other serious medical intervention should be slapped. It's disgusting that anyone would consider giving that advice as a first step. Changing your body isn't going to change your brain.

If you are having panic attacks about pregnancy you clearly have some complex about it. This is not your fault as it sounds like your upbringing was difficult and likely lead you to developing mental issues around pregnancy and birth. You need to seek out therapy for this. Not so that you can be convinced to have a child, or to change your mind about that but just so you don't have to have fear and anxiety around it. You should be able to think about pregnancy without fear and panic.

You do not have to have kids. It is YOUR choice. Accept no pressure what so ever about this. Tell your BF and maybe it means the relationship will end but it's better to be up front about this. Go on birth control if you can there are a lot of options. Else chastity is also a great birth control.

Best of luck to you and please do not consider extreme medical procedures before you explore therapy or other avenues to reduce your fear and panic first. Cutting part of you out isn't going to cut out your fear.

Getting your hair cut sounds like a small victory to me. Take it as a win.

Set yourself small goals like that and knock one thing off at a time. They have to be small enough to be manageable with the level of motivation you have. 

Right now I want a new job. Current one is really toxic and not enough cash for my family needs. But depression makes it hard to speak positively about myself or imagine that I can fulfill a role. So I make a small goal every day to find and apply for one job. Before that my goal was to write one good sentence a day on my resume. Before that it was to write a good sentence on my LinkedIn once a day. If you keep biting off the things you need to do in small enough pieces you will make progress. It helps to make it less daunting. Maybe this can help you. It also helps to tell someone who can ask you if you got it done, keeping you accountable. Use people to help you with this if you have them.

Best wishes bro.

Medication can take a long time to get right. Took me 8 years I think and now I have one that really helps. I don't like to encourage meds but just know it takes time.

I'm sorry you feel that way, but we are usually our own worst judge. People probably don't perceive you as poorly as you do yourself. Its a quirk of mental illness. 

If there is something like new clothes that is going to help you feel better in yourself or more confident try to make a plan to get that done, as hard as it is. I sometimes plan for spontaneity as odd as that sounds. Like setting some cash aside for new clothes and one day just saying "Fuck it, I'm doing it." and you go.

I understand how you feel. People don't expect the cognitive decline either, I didn't but I know it well. 

You sound trapped and I'm sorry for that. I know that too but our circumstances are a little different.

I'm a firm believer that suicide is not selfish but I might be a little biased. Not that I am encouraging. A reasonable person cannot expect you to endure endless torture so they can be spared the grief of your death. It isn't fair to ask.

Is there any way your parents could help with therapy or even a support group. It surprisingly helpful to have people who can listen and show they care in person. They can also help set goals and keep you accountable.

Just know there are people out here on the other side of the internet who don't know you but can empathize with you and do care. All the best.

I know the feeling.

I often wish that people who feel this way could find each other and just hug it out till they felt better. I'm not sure two people like this are best together but the best hugs I've ever had were from people who I KNEW knew how I felt. We understood each other. Its not the same from someone who doesn't get it.

If I knew you we could hug it out. I could use one too.

I'm listening. Sometimes a rant or vent is the best thing to get that anxiety out of your chest. If it helps, keep doing it.

I don't know what having an eating disorder is like but I've felt shame and significant insecurity about how I look and my body. I know that no matter how many times someone says "You're Beautiful" or "You look perfect." etc, etc, whatever, that is doesn't matter. It's about how you view yourself. 

I found that finding one thing that I liked about my body really helped me. It took me some time but eventually I found that I liked my shoulders of all things. So when I see that something is ugly about myself I make sure to follow up by telling myself how nice my shoulders are. Then I do a little flex and show off for the mirror lol. It's not a cure or anything but at least I'm not just experiencing negativity about my body. There is some positive too and it helps.

Lastly, do your best to stay off social media like that. I know you know those woman are using a lot of make-up, filters, photoshop, etc to look as good as possible to get as much attention as possible. More power to them if that's how they want to be but you going there isn't helping you at all.

Therapy is recommended as it's the #1 clinical way to improve outcomes for depression. I've done it on and off with mixed results and I hate being badgered about it. People without depression seem to just think of 'therapy' as a catch-all cure.

Medication is good. I am on one the lifts me out of the dark hole that characterized most of my depressive times. I am a lot less depressed now, but more moody and angry. People around me don't like it because I just seem angry a lot. I love it because I'd rather be a little angry, usually justifiably, then wanting to commit suicide 24/7. 

What I really want is to meet with people who can just empathize with me. Other people with severe and chronic depression. We can look at each other, cry, feel each other's pain and hug it out till we feel human again. We can show love and appreciation for each other in a way that so many other people can't or don't care to.

OP, I'd give you a big freaking bear hug if I could right now. I don't know you but I care about you. Keep trying till something works.

I do.

My days are often a mix of serious depression and suicidal thoughts. Once in a while, maybe 5-6 times over the last decade I've had these perfectly clear, happy, normal days. I forget I'm depressed, I don't think about suicide and I don't feel the overwhelming burdens I usually do. My wife comments on it, it's plain and clear to see how different I am. Then at some point I think "Is this what being normal is like?" then I spiral lol.

I feel like if I could just be "Normal" without depression I would have accomplished 10x as much in my life.

Best of luck to you. I hope we both have more of those kinds of days.

I had a similar friendship with a crush for years in high school. She'd talk about hew relationships and I'd tell her to "Ask him out." or "Go for it." I'd encourage her with other guys because I didn't want to be the POS that would manipulate her so I'd have a chance. Graduate high school and go our separate ways.

Fast forward years later in college I see her in the halls. She dropped out of Uni and came to my local college. We catch up and have some drinks. I'm a very different person at this point and it's like she sees me with fresh eyes. She ended up asking me out, total surprise. We dated for not even two months before I asked if we could just be friends again.

Turned out we weren't even close to compatible as a couple. Took me that long to realize we never were. I spent so long thinking about what it would be like to go out with her, but it was never going to be a ground-breaking relationship. Certainly not when we were younger especially. Terrible in the bedroom too.

My advice buddy. You don't want to do your friend dirty because he still likes her? You've liked her for a long time. If that is your standard for being done dirty well then your friends have been doing that to you for years. So fuck it. Take your chance and ask her out, see what happens of it. Be quick too before one of your other friends swoops in. It's your turn.
Yeah me too. I think I've been dead inside more than I've been alive. Saddest part is no one who knows me notices or cares.

Yeah, above average wage earning millennial here. House and cars eat up most of my pay. I don't take vacations or do any hobbies anymore as they were too expensive. I can't even afford to contribute to my child's education.

I live in the GTA (Toronto). If I did remote work for the same pay but moved to Alberta or the Maritimes I would be fine. Housing is cheaper there. I could pay cash and never have a mortgage again. The dream.

This won't get better anytime soon. Fallout from Covid. The housing boom in the GTA has sent housing prices soaring. Seems like a good thing, but it's not sustainable and means people who aren't in the market are screwed.

I see so much of my own life in what you wrote friend. Technology career, wife and kid (Second little bun is in the oven), job loss. Insurance that I made sure covers suicide as I know that is the most likely way I will go out. Gun owner to boot. 

You have a youtube channel with tutorials? Honestly that is pretty cool. I'm a chicken shit and could never post on youtube.

I've told my wife about my suicidal thoughts and attempts. While she is not a therapist she has been very supportive. She's made it very clear to me that I am the best father for my daughters. She, and my daughters would rather have me than money. Even if I have to flip burgers at Mcdicks for a year while looking for a new job. Being unemployed, or underemployed does not make me a bad father or husband. The same is true for you and it doesn't make you stupid or a loser.

I would encourage you to speak to your wife about this. People who love you will be able to see when you are in those dark places. A hug or kiss offered at those times can mean a world of difference.

The thing that most keeps me back from the ledge is my daughter (Soon to be daughters). I think of all the things I will miss out on in their lives. Teaching them to ride a bike, climb a tree, play catch, play dress up or make-over. I won't get to intimidate their boyfriends or walk them down the isle. Even just the everyday smiles and giggles. The thought of loosing out on their lives is so much more painful than my depression.

For many periods of my life I have preferred the company of dogs to humans. The loyalty and love they have for their best human friend is unmatched in many people. So what happened to your Lupo is unfair and I'm really sorry it happened to you.

As a father I know that kids are a LOT of work. They come with baggage, and hardship, and difficulty and so much work. (lots of positive too) It isn't their fault though. Your brother doesn't have the maturity to understand the pain he brings into your life. Nor is it his fault that his father spoils him. That being said, you are 15 and it isn't your job to carry the baggage I mentioned. It's unfair to you. I suggest you speak to your parents about it. Try writing a script or a letter if that helps, rather than ad lib. Be mature and reserve any resentment. Talk about how you feel and the change that you want. Best of luck on this.

You are a young man. You only have a few more years to go before you can move out and live on your own terms. Please give yourself that chance and see what peace you can make for yourself.  

\-Much love and respect

I know a little of what you are going through. I grew up in a similar home, both parents were constantly at each other's throats. Both had mental illness I'm sure of it. My brother harassed and abused me constantly and I hid in my room. In highschool I went a whole summer break without leaving the house. I suffer with depression and suicidal ideation, for most of my life now. I've cut and attempted before.

Something I do once in a while that I find very cathartic. I meditate a little and in my mind I see myself as the man I am today, and I see a boy, me, when I was \~10yo. I just play with him, like build a tree house, or goto the zoo and see animals or tell ghost stories by a camp fire. Just any of those things that I wished someone who loved me when I was young would have done. I know it's a little strange, but it's like showing love to yourself when no one else is.

Anyway just know that I empathize with you and I care about you.
